mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL YoY and 20-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in Real Final Sales of Goods signals weakening consumer demand, which leads to reduced corporate revenues and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when RSAFS 3-month % change < 0%, or if the correlation between RSAFS 3-month % change and 60-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals labor market weakness, which typically precedes broader economic slowdowns, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE increases > 0.5pp in 1 month, or if the correlation between UNRATE changes and 5-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO MoM > 1%, or if the correlation between INDPRO MoM and 20-day forward returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 5% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) simultaneously rises by more than 0.3 percentage points, it signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when HOUST MoM < -5% and UNRATE > 0.3pp, or if the joint effect of these conditions on 20-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when FEDFUNDS is increasing, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS changes and 60-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points simultaneously, it signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when PAYEMS > 200k and UNRATE < -0.2pp, or if the joint effect of these conditions on 20-day forward returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a decline in GDP (GDPC1) growth rate below 2% year-over-year signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when GDPC1 YoY < 2% during a late-cycle expansion, or if the correlation between GDPC1 YoY and 60-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during this regime.
